title: GCP-6.5: sender-side claim_seq machinery absent (no NVS persistence, no atomic increment-before-claim); Python receiver missing; Rust replay semantics differ
notes: Unblocked: COSE_Sign1 payload format decided (slot-claim-cose-sign1). Sender wraps {iid, superframe, seq, slots} in COSE_Sign1, atomically increments seq in NVS before signing. Agent-implementable.
close_reason: Rust sender-side claim_seq machinery wired: lichend seeds a persisted ClaimSeqStore (gateway-claim-seq.bin) at boot, gated fail-closed (corrupt/unpersistable/missing-on-provisioned all refuse boot; fresh provisioning eagerly anchors counter 0 via new ClaimSeqStore::persist_current so second boot's gate holds). next_claim_seq() is the sole sequence source (increment+persist before sign, GCP-6.5 'Before claim' row). Python sender (ClaimSeqStore slot_claim.py:549) and C NVS receiver (20.1) were already done; Rust store (slot.rs:1095) pre-existed and is now actually wired + regression-tested. 3x reviewer-model codereview converged (3 rounds: correctness, security, edge). Remaining gap filed as follow-up: no production claim-broadcast consumer calls next_claim_seq yet. Pre-existing unrelated end_to_end failure (runtime_ingress_dispatches_authenticated_gcp_slot_claim) verified failing on clean HEAD too.
